headline: Maui Ferry Program

meeting.summary: The county plans to keep Lānaʻi ferry service and expand to Molokaʻi, hoped for by early 2029, with a private company running it.
meeting.recap: A Maui County Department of Transportation staff member opened a community meeting on the proposed Maui Ferry project.[[0:00:03]] Residents said they want an affordable ferry to visit family and reach medical care on Maui.[[0:03:30]] The ferry would carry passengers only, on vessels holding 149 people.[[0:14:34]] A private company would run it under a county contract chosen through a call for bids.[[0:14:51]] Molokaʻi service is hoped for by early 2029.[[0:15:21]] The Maui harbor has not been chosen; the county is waiting to see how the rebuild after the fires goes.[[0:16:46]] The yearly operating cost for Lānaʻi service is estimated at about $5 million, not counting new boats.[[0:20:50]] Ticket sales would cover about 60 percent of that, or about $3 million.[[0:21:26]] The current adult fare to Lānaʻi is $40 one way.[[0:22:37]] The County Council, not the department, will set fares through the budget process.[[0:23:06]] A resident said supplies, including food, ran short on Molokaʻi after a winter storm.[[0:27:36]] Staff said Molokaʻi fares would likely match Lānaʻi fares.[[0:55:13]] Staff said a transportation study of harbor connections will start next month.[[1:02:53]] Residents were asked to fill out a questionnaire through a QR code in the brochure.[[1:09:35]]
meeting.next: The department will pass residents' fare suggestions to the County Council. A draft environmental assessment will be released, and public comments will be added before it is finished. Project updates will be posted on the county website landing page.

moments.q: Question on wheelchair access and ADA rules
"We need these services now. cannot wait till 2029"
